newsitem.title: UK: House of Fraser shrugs off loss, charge news.
newsitem.headline: House of Fraser shrugs off loss, charge news.

text.p: Shares in UK retailer House of Fraser Plc were slightly higher in early dealings on Tuesday after the company announced plans to close stores, a one-off charge and a wider loss in the first half.
House of Fraser rose two pence or 1.2 percent to 164-1/2p by 0800 GMT while the broader market was up 0.25 percent.
Traders said the share, which has failed to keep pace with the market's rise this year, had little downside risk.
"It's no more or no less than what was expected. They admitted they are taking some hits on the restructuring and hopefully all the bad news is now out," one marketmaker said.

House of Fraser said earlier on Tuesday its pretax loss after exceptional charges widened in the first half to 13.6 million stg from 4.3 million a year earlier. It took an exceptional charge of 4.9 million stg.
It said it expected to make provisions of between 40 million and 50 million stg in its full-year accounts for a major reorganisation of its operations.
The company said it "currently envisaged that between five and 10 stores, which over the longer term, are unlikely to meet the group's criteria, may be sold or closed".
Analysts called the figures and statements disappointing.

"The loss before exceptions works out at 8.7 million stg which is certainly worse than one would have thought. The sales mix is wrong with a huge swing towards concession sales...while own-label sales are down," said MiesPierson analyst Nick Bubb.

Bubb said he was likely to cut his forecast for the full year back to 17 million stg profit before exceptionals from 22 million stg expected previously. MeesPierson would continue to recommend selling House of Fraser and switching into Sears Plc.
"It looks like recovery is still a long way off," Bubb said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
